text: Working with APIs is a valuable skill for modern developers. When you interact with an API, you typically send HTTP requests to a server, asking for data or sending information. The server usually responds with JSON, a simple text format that is easy for both computers and humans to read. Before making requests, you often need some form of authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. It’s also important to respect rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a certain time period. Finally, always build error handling into your code. This helps you manage connection problems or unexpected responses without crashing your application.
